source.title: Understanding Machine Unlearning Through the Lens of Mode Connectivity

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether fine-tuning on generic Wikipedia text can undo unlearning, and whether MCU-based parameter averaging changes that outcome. This is a conceptual test of fine-tuning recovery and resistance to relearning attacks.
record.gate_note: The relevant attack result is Figure 6: fine-tuning an unlearned WMDP Cyber model on generic Wikipedia text, followed by evaluation on the WMDP forget set. Other MCU interpolation and mechanism results do not test the listed recovery attacks. Figure 6 gives a plotted trajectory but no extractable numeric values.
record.test_reason: In §5.5 / Figure 6 the study fine-tunes an NPO-unlearned WMDP Cyber model on generic Wikipedia text and reports forget-set accuracy at 20, 40 and 60 relearning steps. This is a benign, unrelated-data relearning attack, which is version B. It also bears on A's claim that simple attacks fail. The same attack is run on the authors' MCU-averaged model, which is a counter-method claim (F). The rest of the paper (mode-connectivity geometry) does not test any listed attack.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct for the attack result. The paper's main conclusions are broader: unlearned models often lie in connected smooth basins; curriculum learning and second-order optimization shift solutions to different basins; basins are functionally heterogeneous on privacy; unlearning is nonlinear ('suppress first, unlearn later') and mostly mechanistically distinct from retraining; MCU ensembling improves forgetting and relearning robustness; and MCU smoothness tracks unlearning difficulty.
record.recipe_differences: The attack fine-tunes on generic Wikipedia text; the compared counter-method averages parameters across multiple MCU minimizers. This is not a test of activation ablation, quantization, or prompt-only attacks.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome depends on whether the unlearned model is standard NPO or NPO with MCU-based averaging; the attack is evaluated at relearning steps labeled 20, 40, and 60.

fits_no_version.finding: Linear interpolation from the original to the unlearned model (§5.3, Fig. 4): verbatim memorization drops before knowledge memorization, which the authors call 'first suppress, then unlearn'.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlearning trajectories suppress surface-form reproduction before removing underlying knowledge (parameter-space interpolation evidence).

fits_no_version.finding: Most approximate unlearning methods are not linearly connected to retrained models on forget metrics; only NPO is (§5.4, Fig. 5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Approximate unlearning reaches solutions mechanistically distinct from retraining.

record.problems: Figure 6 is the only reported attack result, and its numeric values are not stated in the text. The study reports one relearning attack setting (generic Wikipedia text) and does not test the other attack types in the claim.

untested.parts: General ability (MMLU) after the attack is not reported. Whether pre-attack NPO forget accuracy is near chance is not stated in the text.
Relearning on loosely related data or on a subset of the forgotten facts; methods other than NPO; datasets other than WMDP Cyber.
Not tested. There is no activation-direction ablation, and no analysis establishing blocking versus deletion.
Prompting, jailbreaks, other languages and in-context attacks are not tested.
Resistance of MCU averaging to relearning on forget-related data, internal edits, quantization or prompting; other base unlearning methods.

missing.what: Forget-set accuracy for NPO versus the MCU ensemble on WMDP (63.7 vs 24.1 as parsed). This is the pre-attack forget level, relevant to A (near chance) and to the Figure 6 'Unlearn' baseline. Table parsing is ambiguous.
Numeric values of the Figure 6 bars (Original, Unlearn, Relearn20/40/60) for NPO and NPO+MCU. These are needed to gauge the degree of recovery.

record.verdict_notes: The base model for WMDP is not identified. The relearning attack follows Fan et al. (2025). No uncertainty or MMLU utility is reported after the attack. B labels on r4–r6 were removed because those rows test the authors' counter-method (F).

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not report, for the attack result, that targeted accuracy is near chance while general ability is preserved and attacks fail to recover it.
Tests generic Wikipedia fine-tuning as a relearning attack on WMDP Cyber; does not test unrelated/loosely related example sets generally, ablation, quantization, or prompting.
The linear interpolation analysis compares unlearning with retraining, but does not test activation-direction ablation or establish that unlearning blocks access rather than deleting knowledge.
Prompt rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, and in-context information are not tested.
Tests MCU-based averaging against generic-Wikipedia relearning on WMDP Cyber only; does not test resistance to ablation, quantization, or prompting attacks.
